newsitem.title: USA: Genesis Health aims to improve debt ratios.
newsitem.headline: Genesis Health aims to improve debt ratios.

text.p: Genesis Health Ventures Inc, which disclosed earlier this week it was teaming with two investment firms to buy Multicare Co Inc for $1.4 billion, said it was in the midst of various activities to improve its debt ratios.

Genesis Chief Financial Officer George Hager Jr told a Dillon Read analyst meeting: "We have previously expressed our intention to deleverage...These activities are ongoing. We expect $100 million in deleveraging activities to take place by the time the transaction closes."
The deal calls for Genesis based in Kennett Square, Pennsylvania, to join with private investment firms Cypress Group LLC and Texas Pacific Group to start a $28 per share tender offer for Multicare.

Under the agreement, Genesis will invest $300 million in exchange for about 42 percent of the new acquisition venture and Cypress and Texas Pacific will invest $420 million for the remaining 58 percent.

Sources of the $1.4 billion purchase price would be $545 million in senior debt, $200 million in senior subordinated debt and $719 million in equity from Genesis, Cypress and Texas Pacific, Hagar said.
Genesis would buy Multicare's therapy business with cash, using $20 million in Genesis' net after-tax proceeds, he said.
"The new company's debt would be non-recourse to Genesis despite the fact that the acquisition was required to be consolidated," Hagar said.

Genesis will have the option to acquire the equity of the new company from Cypress and Texas Pacific after four years and Cypress and Texas Pacific will have the option to sell the equity of the new company to Genesis after five years.
Hager said the deal also included a five year management agreement to run all of the operations of the new company and a shareholder rights plan.
